main_text.p: suram) in loco ubi accumulant. מָחָק, מַחְקָא Rasio, Expunctio : מוֹחַק Hostorium, lignum, quo mensurae cumulata raduntur.
מָחָר m. Cras: Et synecdochicè pro quovis tempore postero, Posthac, Inposterum, ut Exod.13.14. לְמָחָר In crastinum, Exod.8.10.

מָחֳרַת f. Idem, Num.11.32. לְמָחֳרַת Postero mane, Jon.4. v.7. מִמָּחֳרַת Postridie, Lev.19.6. Et forma constructa, לְמָחֳרַת הַיּוֹם Postridie ejus diei, 1.Par.29.21. מִמָּחֳרַת Idem, Lev.23.11. Aff. לְמָחֳרָתָם Postridie eorum, 1.Sam.30.17.
מְחִיר m. Pretium, 1.Reg.21.2. Aff. מְחִירָהּ Pretium ejus, Job.28.15. Plural. cum Aff. בִּמְחִירֵיהֶם Pretiis eorum, Psal.44.13.

מטא [?] Chald. Advenit, Pervenit, Supervenit, Pertigit: Praet. cum ה, וּמְטָא [?] Et tempus advenit; Dan.7.22. מְטָא [?] Pervenerat; Dan.4.25. וּמְטָת [?] Ut pervenireт, Dan.4. v.19. דִּי מְטָת [?] Quod superventurum est, Dan.4.21. Futur. יִמְטֵא [?] Pertingit, Dan.4.8.
מטט [?] Niph. נִמּוּט Dimoveri, Dilabi. Praeter. בַּל־נִמְּטוּ [?] Ne dimoveantur pedes mei, Psal.17.5.
מטל מָטִיל m. Vectis, Palus: כְּמָטִיל בַּרְזֶל Sicut vectis ferreus, Job.40.13.
מטר מָטָר m. Pluvia, Deuter.11.7. Constr. מְטַר־אַרְצְכֶם Pluviam terræ vestræ, Deut.11.14. Plur. Constr. מִטְרוֹת עֻזּוֹ Pluviæ roboris ejus, Job.37.6.

נִמְטַר Niph. Complui: Futurum, תִּמָּטֵר Complutus fuit, Amos 4.7. Hiph. הִמְטִיר Depluit, Pluviam demisit, Fecit aut sivit ut plueret. Praeter. לֹא הִמְטִיר יְהוָה Non demiserat pluviam Dominus, Gen.2.5. Particip. מַמְטִיר Pluviam demissurus sum, Genes.7.4. Infinit. לְהַמְשִׁיר [?]

page.notes: Hebrew forms marked [?] are hard to read at this scan resolution; vowel points and some consonants are uncertain. "Pertigit" and "Pervenireт" are printed as shown (the last letter of "Pervenireт" is an unusual form, possibly a Cyrillic-like t and may be a printing variant). "Jon.4. v.7." and "Dan.4. v.19." keep the printed space. The Hebrew infinitive at the end of the last entry appears as לְהַמְשִׁיר; the expected form would be לְהַמְטִיר, so this may be a printing error, copied as seen. The first line is a continuation from the previous page's entry (cont="true"). Page number printed at top left as 413.
